shlokas.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन | मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ||1||
shlokas.meaning: Arjuna said: You say I have the right to work only, but never to the fruits of work. Please explain why I should act without attachment.
shlokas.guidance: Focus on action with dedication, not on the outcome.

shlokas.sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | ना तु ते कार्यं कर्मणि सङ्गोऽस्ति न मुक्तिः | कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः ||2||
shlokas.meaning: The Blessed Lord said: Action is inevitable; no one can remain inactive. Seeing inaction in action or action in inaction is the wisdom of the wise.
shlokas.guidance: Understand the subtleties of action and inaction to act wisely.

shlokas.sanskrit: न हि कश्चित्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत् | कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः ||3||
shlokas.meaning: No one can remain without performing action even for a moment; all beings are compelled to act by the qualities born of nature.
shlokas.guidance: Recognize that action is unavoidable; learn to act consciously.

shlokas.sanskrit: एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह य: | अघायुरिन्द्रियक्रियाणि वर्तन्ते नर:
shlokas.meaning: Thus the world is bound by the wheel of action. Everyone’s senses are engaged in action by nature.
shlokas.guidance: Accept the world’s duties and responsibilities while acting mindfully.

shlokas.sanskrit: इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्य बन्धनं मलं | योगिनोऽन्यत्र संशयं कर्म कुर्वन्ति सदा हि ||5||
shlokas.meaning: The senses, mind, and intellect are the bonds that tie one to action. Yogis act with wisdom to avoid bondage.
shlokas.guidance: Use intellect and self-discipline to act without attachment.

shlokas.sanskrit: साङ्ख्यं योगोऽहमित्येतद्वेदितुमिच्छसि | ज्ञानयोगेन प्रपन्नः कर्मफलत्यागी भव ||6||
shlokas.meaning: If you wish to understand me, know that Sankhya (knowledge) and Yoga (action) are connected. One who surrenders through knowledge renounces the fruits of action.
shlokas.guidance: Integrate knowledge and action to rise above attachment.

shlokas.sanskrit: यदा संन्यासस्ते कुलकर्माणि प्रजाश्रितः | त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलसङ्गं न सन्त्येव योगिनाम् ||7||
shlokas.meaning: Even when one renounces action externally, the wise cannot renounce duties entirely; action is inevitable.
shlokas.guidance: Renunciation is inner detachment, not mere inaction.

shlokas.sanskrit: कर्मणो हि मानुषे लोके परं न विद्यते | संन्यासः कर्मणां योगो न हि नास्ति कुतः कथम् ||8||
shlokas.meaning: There is nothing superior to action for humans; renunciation of action is impossible. Yoga is the renunciation of attachment, not action.
shlokas.guidance: Act fully, but with detachment from the results.

shlokas.sanskrit: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय | सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ||9||
shlokas.meaning: Perform your duties established in Yoga, Arjuna, abandoning attachment; remain even-minded in success and failure—this is called Yoga.
shlokas.guidance: Equanimity in all outcomes is the essence of Karma Yoga.

shlokas.sanskrit: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सद्विदां योगमुच्यते | फलत्यागात्कर्मणा योगः प्रवर्तते नरः ||10||
shlokas.meaning: O Arjuna, selfless work done naturally without attachment to results is called Yoga.
shlokas.guidance: Act with sincerity and without expectation for personal gain.

shlokas.sanskrit: अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसंभव: | यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यः यज्ञ: कर्मसमुद्भव: ||11||
shlokas.meaning: Living beings are sustained by food; food comes from rain; rain comes from sacrifice; sacrifice is born of action.
shlokas.guidance: Understand the chain of interdependent actions in life.

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्माद्यज्ञात्सर्वकर्माणि सङ्गमुक्ता: समाचर | अथ त्वं कर्मफलत्यागं यथा कुरुच्युत ||12||
shlokas.meaning: Therefore, perform all actions as sacrifice, free from attachment; relinquish the fruits as I instruct, O Arjuna.
shlokas.guidance: Dedicate all your actions for the greater good without expecting reward.

shlokas.sanskrit: कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म य: | स बुद्धिमान्मनुष्येषु स युक्त: कृत्स्नकर्मकृत् ||13||
shlokas.meaning: One who sees inaction in action, and action in inaction, is wise and disciplined in all deeds.
shlokas.guidance: Act with awareness, understanding the deeper meaning of action and inaction.

shlokas.sanskrit: शरीरवृद्धिं रक्षन्ति भूतानि जनार्दन | भवति तत्र तद्गत: प्राणिनां कर्मफलम् ||14||
shlokas.meaning: Living beings protect their bodies, and the result of their efforts sustains them.
shlokas.guidance: Recognize that work sustains life; act responsibly.

shlokas.sanskrit: कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम् | तस्माद्भावा: संसारस्य मोक्शं प्राप्नोति नरः ||15||
shlokas.meaning: Know that action is born of Brahman, the imperishable; understanding this leads one to liberation from worldly bondage.
shlokas.guidance: Seeing work as divine helps transcend attachment.

shlokas.sanskrit: अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे | गत्वा संप्रवृत्त्यर्थं कर्मण: कर्म करोति य: ||16||
shlokas.meaning: Do not grieve, nor speak words of wisdom improperly; all perform action according to their nature.
shlokas.guidance: Respect the nature and duties of everyone without judgment.

shlokas.sanskrit: कर्मण्यभिप्रवर्तन्ते पुरुषा: प्रकृतिस्था: | प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणै: कर्माणि सर्वश: ||17||
shlokas.meaning: All beings act according to their qualities; actions arise from nature’s inherent modes.
shlokas.guidance: Understand natural tendencies to act wisely and responsibly.

shlokas.sanskrit: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मण: | शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मण: ||18||
shlokas.meaning: Perform your prescribed duty; action is superior to inaction. Even maintaining your body is impossible without action.
shlokas.guidance: Engage in your duties; inaction is not truly possible.

shlokas.sanskrit: यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन | कर्मेन्द्रियै: कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते ||19||
shlokas.meaning: He who controls his senses by the mind, without attachment, achieves Yoga through action.
shlokas.guidance: Self-discipline in action is key to mastery.

shlokas.sanskrit: यस्त्वेतदज्ञानमित्येव मोक्षमार्गमश्नुते | ज्ञाननिष्ठो योगी स च कर्मण्यभिप्रवर्तते ||20||
shlokas.meaning: One who acts with knowledge and devotion progresses toward liberation; the wise yogi engages in action without selfish desire.
shlokas.guidance: Combine knowledge, devotion, and action for spiritual growth.

shlokas.sanskrit: यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः | स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ||21||
shlokas.meaning: Whatever a great person does, others follow; whatever standards they set, the world pursues.
shlokas.guidance: Leaders must act responsibly, as their actions influence society.

shlokas.sanskrit: न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किंचन | नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि ||22||
shlokas.meaning: O Arjuna, there is nothing in the three worlds that I must do, nor anything unattained, yet I continue to act.
shlokas.guidance: Selfless action is performed not out of need, but to uphold balance.

shlokas.sanskrit: यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः | मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ||23||
shlokas.meaning: If I ever ceased to act, all people would follow my path and fall into inactivity.
shlokas.guidance: Duty-bound action preserves order in the world.

shlokas.sanskrit: उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम् | सङ्करस्य च कर्ता स्यामुपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः ||24||
shlokas.meaning: If I did not perform action, these worlds would perish, social chaos would arise, and beings would be destroyed.
shlokas.guidance: Neglect of responsibility leads to societal collapse.

shlokas.sanskrit: सक्ताः कर्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्वन्ति भारत | कुर्याद्विद्वांस्तथासक्तश्चिकीर्षुर्लोकसंग्रहम् ||25||
shlokas.meaning: As ignorant people act with attachment, the wise should act without attachment, for the welfare of the world.
shlokas.guidance: Act selflessly to guide others toward balance and harmony.

shlokas.sanskrit: न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम् | जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान्युक्तः समाचरन् ||26||
shlokas.meaning: The wise should not disturb the minds of the ignorant attached to action, but should inspire them through example.
shlokas.guidance: Teach through conduct, not confrontation.

shlokas.sanskrit: प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः | अहंकारविमूढात्मा कर्ताहमिति मन्यते ||27||
shlokas.meaning: All actions are performed by the qualities of nature, but the deluded ego thinks, 'I am the doer.'
shlokas.guidance: Release ego to gain clarity and humility.

shlokas.sanskrit: तत्त्ववित्तु महाबाहो गुणकर्मविभागयोः | गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते ||28||
shlokas.meaning: One who knows the truth understands that qualities act upon qualities and remains unattached.
shlokas.guidance: Awareness of nature’s play frees one from attachment.

shlokas.sanskrit: प्रकृतेर्गुणसम्मूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्मसु | तानकृत्स्नविदो मन्दान्कृत्स्नविन्न विचालयेत् ||29||
shlokas.meaning: Those deluded by nature’s qualities cling to action; the wise should not unsettle them.
shlokas.guidance: Compassion is essential when guiding others.

shlokas.sanskrit: मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा | निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः ||30||
shlokas.meaning: Dedicate all actions to Me, free from desire and ego, and fight without anxiety.
shlokas.guidance: Surrender anxiety by dedicating action to a higher purpose.

shlokas.sanskrit: ये मे मतमिदं नित्यमनुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः | श्रद्धावन्तोऽनसूयन्तो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि कर्मभिः ||31||
shlokas.meaning: Those who follow this teaching with faith and without resentment are freed from bondage of action.
shlokas.guidance: Faith and humility lead to liberation.

shlokas.sanskrit: ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम् | सर्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्विद्धि नष्टानचेतसः ||32||
shlokas.meaning: Those who criticize and do not follow this teaching are deluded and spiritually lost.
shlokas.guidance: Ego-driven rejection of wisdom leads to stagnation.

shlokas.sanskrit: सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि | प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति ||33||
shlokas.meaning: Even the wise act according to their nature; beings follow their nature—what can restraint accomplish?
shlokas.guidance: Understand and work with nature, not against it.

shlokas.sanskrit: इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ | तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ ||34||
shlokas.meaning: Attraction and aversion arise from senses; one should not fall under their control.
shlokas.guidance: Master desires to avoid inner conflict.

shlokas.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् | स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ||35||
shlokas.meaning: Better to perform one’s own duty imperfectly than another’s perfectly; another’s duty brings fear.
shlokas.guidance: Stay true to your own path.

shlokas.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच | अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः ||36||
shlokas.meaning: Arjuna asked: What compels a person to commit sin, even against their will?
shlokas.guidance: Understanding the root of wrongdoing is essential for mastery.

shlokas.sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः ||37||
shlokas.meaning: The Lord said: It is desire and anger, born of passion, that compels sinful action.
shlokas.guidance: Unchecked desire transforms into destructive anger.

shlokas.sanskrit: धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथादर्शो मलेन च | यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम् ||38||
shlokas.meaning: Just as fire is covered by smoke or a mirror by dust, knowledge is covered by desire.
shlokas.guidance: Remove desire to reveal inner wisdom.

shlokas.sanskrit: आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा | कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च ||39||
shlokas.meaning: Knowledge is obscured by insatiable desire, the eternal enemy of the wise.
shlokas.guidance: Awareness weakens desire’s grip.

shlokas.sanskrit: इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते | एतैर्विमोहयत्येष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम् ||40||
shlokas.meaning: The senses, mind, and intellect are its seat; through them desire deludes the soul.
shlokas.guidance: Guard the mind to protect wisdom.

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ | पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम् ||41||
shlokas.meaning: Therefore, first control the senses and destroy this sinful desire that destroys wisdom.
shlokas.guidance: Self-control is the foundation of growth.

shlokas.sanskrit: इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः | मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः ||42||
shlokas.meaning: The senses are superior to matter, the mind superior to senses, intellect superior to mind, and the Self superior to intellect.
shlokas.guidance: Rise step by step toward the higher Self.

shlokas.sanskrit: एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना | जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम् ||43||
shlokas.meaning: Knowing the Self beyond intellect, steady the mind and conquer desire, the formidable enemy.
shlokas.guidance: Self-realization is the ultimate victory.
